headline: Medium prompt-injection and data-leakage risk from Copilot editing shared repo context into Khoj’s broad-reach retrieval pipeline.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Copilot reads repo context and open editor buffers, and can propose edits for human review; Khoj reads indexed personal notes/files and has broad network egress. If Copilot-generated content is copied into Khoj or indexed alongside notes, malicious instructions can persist and be re-surfaced. The shared path is plausible, but not default automatic ingestion, so medium fits.
conditions: IF Copilot output is copied into Khoj-indexed notes or documents
IF Khoj retrieval surfaces Copilot-authored text as authoritative instructions
mitigations: Review Copilot output before copying into notes
Tag Copilot-generated text as untrusted in Khoj
Exclude prompt-like files from Khoj indexing
Use a separate workspace for AI-generated drafts
requires-engineering: add provenance labels to indexed content

B_data_leakage.rationale: Copilot touches source code and open editor buffers, while Khoj indexes personal notes/files and may use cloud or self-hosted servers. A shared workspace or copied content can move sensitive code or notes between them. The profiles do not show automatic shared storage, so leakage is plausible but not default; medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF the same directory contains source code and personal notes
IF Copilot-generated code or comments are indexed by Khoj
mitigations: Keep code and personal notes in separate folders
Disable indexing for repositories with secrets
Audit Khoj’s indexed sources today
Remove sensitive snippets from shared notes
requires-engineering: enforce per-folder indexing allowlists

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Copilot can write the filesystem and modify git state; Khoj cannot write files or modify git state. Their write surfaces do not overlap, so direct conflict is limited. The main risk is indirect contention through shared files, which is unusual rather than default, so low is sufficient.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable working tree
IF a human applies Copilot edits while Khoj simultaneously indexes the same files
mitigations: Avoid concurrent edits in the same folder
Pause indexing during large code changes
Commit Copilot changes before re-indexing
Use separate git branches for AI-assisted work
requires-engineering: add file-lock coordination

D_cascading_error.rationale: Copilot produces edits for human review, and Khoj can retrieve and present indexed text. If Copilot output is stored in notes or docs, Khoj may later surface it as context without verification. Because Copilot is not automatically acting on Khoj output and human review exists, the cascade is real but not high.
conditions: IF Copilot-generated text is saved into Khoj’s indexed corpus
IF a user treats Khoj retrieval as verified truth without checking the source
mitigations: Mark AI-generated notes as draft
Require source links in retrieved summaries
Manually verify any retrieved code or facts
Keep task instructions out of long-term notes
requires-engineering: add source-confidence scoring

E_compliance.rationale: Copilot is vendor-hosted with GitHub repo context, while Khoj may be self-hosted or use cloud/search providers and stores personal notes plus model API keys. If regulated code or personal data is moved between them, retention and residency policies can diverge. The profiles do not prove a specific legal mismatch, so medium is the cautious choice.
conditions: IF personal data or regulated source code is indexed by Khoj
IF GitHub-hosted Copilot context includes data subject to stricter retention rules
mitigations: Classify data before indexing
Keep regulated data out of Khoj
Review vendor retention settings today
Use self-hosted Khoj for sensitive corpora
requires-engineering: document residency and retention boundaries
